task.goal: Make a small clinic's appointment reminder process more reliable when text messages sometimes fail, without increasing privacy exposure.
hard_constraints: Use existing scheduling software export and a staffed phone line; no new vendor or patient app.
A reminder must not reveal clinical details, and opt-outs must be honored.
Two clerks have 30 minutes daily; distinguish bad phone numbers, delivery failure and response failure; report how missed appointments and unwanted contact would be measured.
task.available_resources: Aggregate delivery status and existing consent records.
task.expected_result: An operational fallback workflow with privacy and workload checks.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Confirmation-based exception queue with capped phone fallback
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Use missing confirmation to trigger a phone fallback. Export upcoming appointments and join them locally to existing consent and opt-out records using an internal appointment identifier. Send the existing neutral text only where permitted, with a confirmation route through the staffed phone line or an existing reply function. Confirmation is optional; silence never cancels an appointment.

Each morning, clerks work a single exception queue, prioritizing appointments occurring soonest. Keep three separate classifications: bad number means an invalid-number indication or a person explicitly reporting a wrong number; delivery failure means a technical delivery failure, attributable to an appointment only if existing software supplies that information; response failure means no confirmation by the cutoff, with delivery unknown where applicable. Aggregate delivery statistics cannot identify individual failed messages, so do not label silent patients as delivery failures.

Make at most one fallback call per appointment, only when telephone contact is permitted. Verify the intended recipient before discussing appointment logistics. Leave a generic callback message only where existing consent allows it; disclose no clinical details, and consider whether naming the clinic itself creates exposure. Apply opt-outs before each contact, distinguish channel-specific from all-reminder opt-outs, and stop after a wrong-number report.

The daily budget is 60 clerk-minutes: reserve 10 for export, consent checks and reconciliation, 40 for calls, and 10 for recording outcomes. Set the call cap from observed handling time; record overflow rather than adding work. Keep the queue in existing approved storage, restrict access, and remove temporary exports under existing retention rules. This needs existing confirmation tracking or a minimal approved local log. It may miss patients when the queue exceeds capacity.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: Pilot against the current text-only process using comparable appointment groups, ideally randomized if operationally feasible. First inspect a small queue to verify consent filtering and classification without making extra contacts. Record clerk-minutes, queue overflow, confirmations and completed calls. Measure missed appointments as no-shows divided by eligible booked appointments, reporting cancellations separately. Measure unwanted contact through opt-out violations, wrong-person contacts, complaints and patient reports of unwanted reminders, with contact attempts as the denominator. The mechanism is undermined if confirmations do not identify a manageable group, workload exceeds 60 minutes daily, or no-shows do not improve without increased unwanted contact. A small pilot checks feasibility, not a definitive effect.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Patient-chosen phone reminders that bypass unreliable texts
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Change the primary reminder channel for patients who prefer telephone contact or report unreliable texting, instead of adding calls after every unanswered text. During an already occurring booking, check-in or patient-initiated call, staff verify the contact number privately, check existing consent, and offer either the existing text reminder, one telephone reminder, or no reminder. Do not make extra outreach merely to recruit patients. Record the selection in existing scheduling fields if available; otherwise use a minimal access-controlled list linked by internal appointment identifier.

The daily export creates mutually exclusive text and telephone lists. Phone-selected patients receive one call from the staffed line, replacing the text. The clerk verifies the recipient before giving appointment logistics, excludes clinical details, and leaves only an approved generic callback message when voicemail permission exists. A wrong-number report immediately suppresses that number pending verification through a legitimate patient interaction. Honor channel-specific and overall opt-outs before generating and again before executing the list.

Keep distinct outcomes: bad number for explicit invalidity or a wrong recipient; delivery failure for an identified technical failure; response failure for an unanswered call or an unconfirmed reminder. Report aggregate text failures separately because they cannot establish which patient experienced failure. Neither an unanswered call nor missing text confirmation proves a bad number.

Allocate the combined 60 daily clerk-minutes to 10 minutes of list preparation and consent checks, 40 minutes of calls, and 10 minutes of reconciliation. Limit telephone enrollment using measured call duration and expected daily appointments; check capacity before promising that service. This requires existing software to record preferences and suppress duplicate reminders. It works by moving a bounded group off the unreliable channel, but uptake and successful telephone reach are uncertain. It does not automatically rescue failures among patients retaining text reminders.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: Start with a small consenting group whose telephone volume fits the daily cap. Compare their subsequent attendance and contact burden with their own recent text-reminder appointments, while reporting differences in appointment type and timing that could confound the comparison. Inspect exports for duplicate channel assignments and stale opt-outs before launch. Track handling time, unanswered calls, bad numbers, technical failures and capacity overruns separately. Measure no-shows per eligible appointment, cancellations separately, and unwanted contacts through wrong recipients, opt-out breaches, complaints and reported unwanted reminders per attempt. Reject or revise the approach if telephone reach is no better, attendance shows no useful signal, or privacy incidents or workload increase. A larger comparison would be needed to establish effectiveness.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Aggregate outage trigger with a bounded phone contingency
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Use aggregate delivery deterioration to activate a telephone contingency for an affected appointment batch, rather than treating individual silence as evidence of failure. This targets a shared texting disruption; it cannot identify which patients missed a text.

First inspect whether existing delivery reports identify a sending period and include attempted and failed message counts. Compare each completed period with recent comparable periods, allowing for delayed statuses. Set a provisional activation threshold from that baseline. If reports cannot distinguish periods or lack meaningful counts, this mechanism is not usable.

When the threshold is crossed, export the corresponding upcoming appointments. Filter against current telephone consent and all-reminder opt-outs, and remove appointments already confirmed where that information exists. Prioritize imminent appointments, rotating equal-priority records to avoid repeatedly favoring the same patients. Make at most one fallback call per appointment, checking consent again immediately before dialing. Silence never cancels a booking. Verify the recipient before giving appointment logistics; disclose no clinical details. Leave only a generic callback message where permission exists, considering whether identifying the clinic itself is sensitive.

Maintain separate outcomes: bad number requires an explicit invalid-number indication or wrong-recipient report; delivery failure remains an aggregate text count unless individually attributable; response failure means an unanswered call or no confirmation, with text delivery unknown. Suppress reported wrong numbers pending legitimate verification.

The two clerks share 60 minutes daily: 10 for status and consent checks, 40 for calls, and 10 for reconciliation. Set the call cap from observed handling time and record overflow. Use approved existing storage and retention rules. This assumes exports can be matched to reporting periods. It may waste calls on successfully delivered texts and miss isolated failures during otherwise normal periods.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: Inspect one historical or current reporting period without contacting patients to verify batch matching, consent filtering and a feasible call count. Then, during a triggered period, randomly allocate eligible appointments to capped fallback calls or the existing text-only process. Record clerk-minutes, overflow and successful reach. Measure missed appointments as no-shows per eligible booked appointment, reporting cancellations separately. Measure unwanted contact using wrong-person contacts, opt-out breaches, complaints and reported unwanted reminders, reporting both counts and rates per attempt. Stop and correct any privacy breach. Poor batch attribution, workload overruns or little additional reach would falsify operational feasibility; attendance effects require more observations.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Repair contact records before reminders, with phone replacement after late corrections
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Reduce preventable text failures by correcting contact records during interactions already taking place. At booking, check-in or a patient-initiated call, staff privately ask patients to verify their own number and existing reminder permissions. Do not read a stored number aloud in a public area or treat verification as new consent. Correct verified errors in the existing scheduling record; suppress explicitly reported wrong numbers until legitimately reverified.

Use the daily appointment export to identify upcoming appointments whose contact details were corrected during those interactions. A minimal restricted log of internal appointment identifiers and correction dates is needed if existing software cannot export changes. Check whether the existing reminder is still scheduled to use the corrected record. If the normal sending cutoff has passed, place one replacement reminder call from the staffed line where telephone consent permits. Do not initiate additional texts unless existing software supports doing so and staff can exclude duplicates. Silence never cancels an appointment.

Before dialing, recheck opt-outs. Verify the recipient before providing appointment logistics, disclose no clinical details, and leave a generic callback message only under existing voicemail permission. Consider whether identifying the clinic itself is sensitive.

Keep three distinct outcomes: bad number requires verified invalidity or an explicit wrong-recipient report; delivery failure uses aggregate technical status and cannot be attributed to an individual; response failure means an unanswered call or absent confirmation, with text delivery unknown.

Allocate each clerk’s 30 minutes as five minutes of reconciliation, twenty minutes of calls and five minutes of logging. Cap calls using observed handling time and record overflow. Include incremental verification time in the workload accounting. This requires editable contact records and a way to establish the reminder cutoff. It could prevent recurring failures from stale data, but cannot repair network outages or guarantee timely rescue when patients have no intervening interaction.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: First inspect a small upcoming export and existing reminder settings to establish whether corrected numbers actually feed pending reminders. Compare the workflow with usual practice over a short pilot, counting verified corrections, replacement calls, successful reach, duplicate contacts, clerk time and overflow. Do not withhold known corrections for comparison. Measure no-shows per eligible booked appointment, reporting cancellations separately; a historical comparison provides only a weak attendance signal. Measure unwanted contact through wrong-recipient contacts, opt-out violations, complaints and patient reports, reporting counts and rates per attempt. Few actionable corrections, unchanged downstream contact records or workload exceeding 60 clerk-minutes daily would undermine this mechanism. Aggregate delivery improvement alone would not establish causation.

EXPAND.title: Patient-initiated reminder check through the existing phone line
EXPAND.proposal:
Make the staffed phone line an agreed backup that patients initiate when a text does not arrive. During an already occurring booking or check-in, offer a simple instruction: if the expected reminder has not arrived by an agreed time, call the existing clinic number during staffed hours. Give the appointment details at booking as usual; the text remains an optional convenience. Participation is voluntary, and failure to call never cancels an appointment. This changes the recovery mechanism from staff identifying failed texts to patients reporting missing reminders, without additional outbound contact.

Use the scheduling export to reconcile incoming checks against current appointments. Verify the caller using the clinic's existing procedure before discussing appointment logistics; disclose no clinical details in reminders. Do not solicit clinical information in voicemail. Honor existing reminder opt-outs and make no unsolicited return call unless permitted. Record only the minimum outcome in approved existing storage, following existing access and retention rules.

Keep three distinct categories: bad number requires an explicit invalid-number indication or wrong-recipient report; delivery failure is reported at aggregate level unless the existing system provides attributable evidence; response failure means an agreed check-in was not received by its cutoff. A patient reporting no text is a reported nonreceipt, not proof of technical delivery failure. Suppress explicitly wrong numbers pending legitimate verification.

The two clerks each retain a 30-minute daily limit: together allocate 10 minutes to export and consent checks, 40 to handling backup calls, and 10 to reconciliation. Limit enrollment using observed handling time and monitor unanswered incoming calls. Prerequisites are an existing way to record participation and enough staffed-line capacity. The approach depends on patients remembering the backup instruction and being able to call; it cannot reliably rescue patients who do neither.
EXPAND.experiment: Offer the backup to a small, capacity-limited group over comparable appointment periods, using the current text-only process as the comparator. Count missed appointments among all appointments offered the backup, not just callers, and record cancellations separately. Measure unwanted contact through wrong-recipient contacts, contact despite opt-out, and patient complaints, with reminder attempts as the denominator. Record clerk minutes, incoming calls answered and abandoned where observable, and missing-text reports resolved before the appointment. Inspect aggregate delivery failures separately. The mechanism is undermined if patients reporting missing texts rarely use the line, callers cannot get through, workload exceeds 60 clerk-minutes, or missed appointments do not improve. A small trial can expose operational failure but cannot establish a reliable effect on missed appointments.

REFINE.title: Candidate 2 repair: freeze the reminder cohort before an outage
REFINE.proposal: Original candidate 2 is the strongest fit because it uses the available aggregate delivery evidence without assuming individual delivery tracking. Its specific weakness is reconstructing an affected sending batch from a later appointment export: rescheduling, cancellations and new bookings can make that export include patients outside the batch or omit patients within it. Change one action: retain a minimal, access-controlled snapshot of internal appointment identifiers for each existing reminder run, linked to its aggregate reporting period. When the outage threshold triggers, reconcile that snapshot against current appointments, consent and opt-outs before creating the capped telephone queue. Exclude cancelled appointments and records whose reminder eligibility cannot be resolved. This makes the fallback target the actual affected cohort and reduces unnecessary calls. Prerequisites are an export that identifies the reminder-run cohort and delivery reports covering that same cohort; a list of merely upcoming appointments is insufficient. Preserve the original 60 clerk-minute budget, one-call limit, recipient verification, neutral content and voicemail permissions. Record bad numbers only with explicit evidence, technical delivery failures at aggregate level, and unanswered calls separately as response failures. Remaining limit: successful text recipients within the affected cohort may still receive a call, and isolated failures outside triggered batches remain unaddressed.
REFINE.experiment: Run one contact-free rehearsal: snapshot a reminder cohort, then reconcile it after a cancellation, reschedule and opt-out, using approved test records if available. Verify that the aggregate reporting period maps to that cohort, excluded records cannot enter the call queue, and preparation plus reconciliation fits the reserved 20 clerk-minutes. Inability to establish cohort membership falsifies this repair. During a capped pilot, measure no-shows per eligible booked appointment against the existing text-only process, reporting cancellations separately; count wrong-person contacts, opt-out breaches, complaints and reported unwanted reminders both absolutely and per contact attempt. Record total clerk-minutes and overflow to check the 60-minute daily limit.

Verify the recipient before giving appointment logistics; disclose no clinical details. Leave only a generic callback message where permission exists, considering whether identifying the clinic itself is sensitive.

Maintain separate outcomes: bad number requires an explicit invalid-number indication or wrong-recipient report; delivery failure remains an aggregate text count unless individually attributable; response failure means an unanswered call or no confirmation, with text delivery unknown. Suppress reported wrong numbers pending legitimate verification.

The two clerks share 60 minutes daily: 10 for status and consent checks, 40 for calls, and 10 for reconciliation. Set the call cap from observed handling time and record overflow. Use approved existing storage and retention rules. This assumes exports can be matched to reporting periods. It may waste calls on successfully delivered texts and miss isolated failures during otherwise normal periods.
SAVE.experiment: Inspect one historical or current reporting period without contacting patients to verify batch matching, consent filtering and a feasible call count. Then, during a triggered period, randomly allocate eligible appointments to capped fallback calls or the existing text-only process. Record clerk-minutes, overflow and successful reach. Measure missed appointments as no-shows per eligible booked appointment, reporting cancellations separately. Measure unwanted contact using wrong-person contacts, opt-out breaches, complaints and reported unwanted reminders, reporting both counts and rates per attempt. Stop and correct any privacy breach. Poor batch attribution, workload overruns or little additional reach would falsify operational feasibility; attendance effects require more observations.

SAVE.title: Repair contact records before reminders, with phone replacement after late corrections
SAVE.proposal:
Reduce preventable text failures by correcting contact records during interactions already taking place. At booking, check-in or a patient-initiated call, staff privately ask patients to verify their own number and existing reminder permissions. Do not read a stored number aloud in a public area or treat verification as new consent. Correct verified errors in the existing scheduling record; suppress explicitly reported wrong numbers until legitimately reverified.

Use the daily appointment export to identify upcoming appointments whose contact details were corrected during those interactions. A minimal restricted log of internal appointment identifiers and correction dates is needed if existing software cannot export changes. Check whether the existing reminder is still scheduled to use the corrected record. If the normal sending cutoff has passed, place one replacement reminder call from the staffed line where telephone consent permits. Do not initiate additional texts unless existing software supports doing so and staff can exclude duplicates. Silence never cancels an appointment.

Before dialing, recheck opt-outs. Verify the recipient before providing appointment logistics, disclose no clinical details, and leave a generic callback message only under existing voicemail permission. Consider whether identifying the clinic itself is sensitive.

Keep three distinct outcomes: bad number requires verified invalidity or an explicit wrong-recipient report; delivery failure uses aggregate technical status and cannot be attributed to an individual; response failure means an unanswered call or absent confirmation, with text delivery unknown.

Allocate each clerk’s 30 minutes as five minutes of reconciliation, twenty minutes of calls and five minutes of logging. Cap calls using observed handling time and record overflow. Include incremental verification time in the workload accounting. This requires editable contact records and a way to establish the reminder cutoff. It could prevent recurring failures from stale data, but cannot repair network outages or guarantee timely rescue when patients have no intervening interaction.
SAVE.experiment: First inspect a small upcoming export and existing reminder settings to establish whether corrected numbers actually feed pending reminders. Compare the workflow with usual practice over a short pilot, counting verified corrections, replacement calls, successful reach, duplicate contacts, clerk time and overflow. Do not withhold known corrections for comparison. Measure no-shows per eligible booked appointment, reporting cancellations separately; a historical comparison provides only a weak attendance signal. Measure unwanted contact through wrong-recipient contacts, opt-out violations, complaints and patient reports, reporting counts and rates per attempt. Few actionable corrections, unchanged downstream contact records or workload exceeding 60 clerk-minutes daily would undermine this mechanism. Aggregate delivery improvement alone would not establish causation.
